title: Longest Run of Ones with K Flips
statement: You are given a binary list nums that contains only the integers 0 and 1, and a non-negative integer k. You are allowed to flip at most k of the zeros into ones (you may flip fewer, or none). Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray that consists entirely of ones after performing your flips. A subarray is valid to consider while it contains at most k zeros, since those zeros are exactly the ones you would flip. Return the answer as an int. If nums is empty, return 0.
hints: You are looking for the longest contiguous stretch that satisfies a budget constraint (at most k zeros). What technique lets you grow and shrink a contiguous range without re-scanning it?
Keep a window [left, right] and a running count of zeros inside it. The window is valid exactly when that count is at most k; track the best width you have ever seen while valid.

Advance right one step at a time, incrementing the zero count when nums[right] is 0. Whenever the count exceeds k, slide left forward one position at a time, decrementing the count each time the element leaving at nums[left] is a 0, until the window is valid again. Do not reset left to right and do not forget to decrement on exit; after fixing the window, update best with right - left + 1.
